title: Paris
completionText: You return to London with trunks full of engravings, debts in three currencies, and a permanent taste for chocolate. The Grand Tour is complete.

cards.dialogue: "Your coach rumbles down the Faubourg Saint-Honoré. After Rome's grandeur and Venice's secrets, Paris greets you with mud, perfume, and a thousand pamphlets thrust through the carriage window."
cards.leftChoice: An inn on the Left Bank
cards.leftText: You lodge above a bookseller in the Rue Saint-Jacques. Your landlady mends Diderot's stockings.
cards.rightText: The Hôtel de Bourbon is in the rue des Petits-Augustins. Your valet is poached from a duke within the week.

cards.dialogue: "A presentation at Versailles requires a sword, silk stockings of the proper length, and a sponsor of suitable rank. Lord Albemarle's name may suffice — and a thousand livres for the tailor, more for the chamberlain."
cards.leftText: You view Versailles on a Sunday with the public crowd, jostled by butchers' wives admiring the parquet.
cards.rightText: His Most Christian Majesty Louis XV notices you for perhaps three seconds. You will speak of it for years.

cards.dialogue: "On Mondays I receive the artists, on Wednesdays the philosophes. Monsieur d'Alembert quarrelled with the Abbé Morellet last week over the nature of free will. The wit is sharp here — bring your own."
cards.leftText: You take careful notes. Madame Geoffrin nods approvingly: the silent Englishman is always welcome.
cards.rightText: You defend Hume against Diderot, badly. The room laughs but invites you back.

cards.dialogue: "You wish to call on Monsieur de Voltaire at Ferney, signore? The road is long, his temper short — but he reads English, remembers London fondly, and treats serious visitors to dinner and an hour of his views."
cards.leftText: You stay in Paris and visit the Encyclopédie offices instead. Diderot lends you a draft of his article on Genève.
cards.rightText: Voltaire is small, sharp, and astonishingly alive at seventy. He gives you Candide, inscribed.

cards.dialogue: "The Opéra plays Rameau tonight — Castor et Pollux, with the new scenery. A seat in the parterre costs almost nothing, but the Duchesse de Gramont's loge requires a different kind of currency, signore."
cards.leftText: You stand among Paris's clerks and students. They sing along loudly in the wrong key. The music survives.
cards.rightText: The Duchesse is gracious, the Opera magnificent. By the third act you are introduced to half the Faubourg Saint-Germain.

cards.dialogue: "Monsieur le Vicomte demands satisfaction for the remark made over cards last night. Tomorrow at dawn, by the Bois de Boulogne. Pistols, regrettably — Paris no longer tolerates blades drawn in public."
cards.leftText: Your apology is read aloud at the Café Procope. You are advised to leave Paris before Lent.
cards.rightText: The Vicomte's ball passes through your hat. Yours nicks his shoulder. Both honour and your shirts are saved.
